title: Book Three · Chapter 125: Three Mornings
story:
Spring passes, and the summer holiday begins.

Dad and Mr Sun have changed the order of his work. He spends shorter stretches at the bench. Between them, he measures finished pieces or checks the work near the counter.

His hands still ache some evenings. They feel better on many days.

On Friday afternoon, Ronan walks to the workshop with him. Dad needs to return a drawing after lunch. Ronan wants to ask about holiday work.

Mr Sun is near the front table. He listens while Ronan explains.

“For the whole holiday?”

“Part of it. I want to try real work.”

Mr Sun looks at his list.

“I could use help at the front. There is paper to sort. Customers bring sizes, and someone needs to write them clearly.”

“I can do that.”

“Some of it,” Dad says.

Ronan looks at him, then smiles. “I can learn the rest.”

Mr Sun shows him the counter and the low measuring table. Behind them, an adult worker is cutting wood. Ronan stays at the front while Mr Sun points out the work there.

“These are yours. The cutting stays with us.”

Ronan nods. A customer comes in with a small drawer. Mr Sun puts it on the counter and writes down her name.

Ronan watches him ask about the problem. The woman points to one side. Mr Sun checks it himself before he mentions a date.

After she leaves, he turns back to Ronan.

“Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Nine until twelve. Four weeks to start.”

Ronan counts the mornings on his fingers. Twelve in all. He will work three hours each morning.

“Two yuan for a morning,” Mr Sun says. “Six each Friday, after the three mornings.”

“All right.”

“Come this Monday. You can start with the front shelves.”

Ronan writes the days and times on a small piece of paper. Mr Sun checks it and hands it back.

Outside, Dad stops beside him.

“Still want to come?”

“Yes.”

“The paper won't always laugh at your voices.”

“The customers might.”

Dad smiles. Then he goes back through the workshop door with his drawing. Ronan folds his own paper and puts it in his pocket.

At home, he tells Mum about the twelve mornings. She asks about the afternoons.

“School work. Anna. Football.”

“All three every day?”

“I may need another afternoon.”

She laughs and pours him some water. He takes the paper out once more and writes Monday at the top.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

workshop＝作坊、工作间；counter＝接待柜台；ache＝隐隐酸痛；sort＝分类整理。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan约定每周哪几天、几点至几点工作？四周共有多少个上午？
2. 每上午和每周报酬各是多少？哪些工作留给成人？

## 读句子

**He will work three hours each morning.**

拆开看：He / will work / three hours / each morning.

他／将工作／三个小时／每个工作日上午。
